hooks: Morning. A resident reports a leak under the sink.
Your resident just explained the same problem twice today.
Day shift knew. Night shift did not. The resident paid for it.
script: Morning. A resident reports a leak under the sink. Day shift logs it, tries the easy fix, clocks out. Evening. The resident calls back. Different person. "Can you explain what happened?" Nothing was lost. It was just sitting somewhere else. A useful handoff keeps four things together: the request, what was tried, who owns it, the next action. The next person picks it up mid-sentence. Where does your team lose the thread between shifts?
